title: TODAY I WILL BEGIN TO EXALT YOU

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And the Lord said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you in the eyes of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses. Tell the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan's waters, go and stand in the river.'" — Josh 3:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Joshua He is about to lift him up in the eyes of the people. But notice why: "so they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses." God was not exalting Joshua for Joshua's sake, to make him proud or famous. He was confirming Joshua's leadership so the people would trust God's chosen guide and follow with confidence.

This is a healthy way to think about honour and influence. Any position God gives us is never merely for our own glory. It is so that others may see God at work and be pointed back to Him. When God lifts someone up, it is meant to build the faith of the whole community, not the ego of one person.

There is also great tenderness here for Joshua. Stepping into Moses' huge shoes must have been daunting. God graciously reassures him: "I am with you as I was with Moses." The same God, the same presence, the same power. Joshua did not need to be Moses; he only needed the God of Moses.

The command about standing in the river reminds us again that God's promises meet us as we obey. Ultimately, all true exaltation belongs to Christ, whom God has raised to the highest place (Phil 2:9). Any honour we receive is only to reflect glory back to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When God gives you influence, do you use it to point people to Him?
2. Do you ever feel you have to fill someone else's "shoes"? How does God's promise here help?
3. Are you seeking your own glory, or God's glory through your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, whatever place You give me, let it point others to You. Reassure me that Your presence is enough, and let all honour return to Christ. Amen.
